endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Data management must be grounded in an effective data mapping exercise and a strong, clear, and efficient data governance process.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Note that not all organizations will be using data to develop or train models, but must still have data preparation SOPs for data that will be input into the model for use, used to fine-tune the model, or shared with third-party vendors.

endorsements.title: Developing, purchasing, implementing and monitoring AI tools in radiology: practical considerations. A multi-society statement
endorsements.issuer: ACR, CAR, ESR, RANZCR, RSNA; Radiol Artif Intell 2024 (PMID 38251899, doi:10.1148/ryai.230513)
endorsements.quote: A local AI champion plays a significant role in promoting AI adoption among radiologists.

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Consider the following factors when updating or defining risk tiers for GAI: Abuses and impacts to information integrity; Dependencies between GAI and other IT or data systems; Harm to fundamental rights or public safety

endorsements.title: Federated data health networks hold potential for accelerating emergency research
endorsements.issuer: Journal of the American College of Emergency Physicians open
endorsements.quote: Guidelines for the creation of a successful FDHN have been developed by the World Economic Forum and requires the commitment of site resources, the development of a robust data governance structure to address compliance with regulatory requirements and collaboration with health information technology personnel for data quality assurance.

endorsements.title: SAGES consensus recommendations on surgical video data use, structure, and exploration (for research in artificial intelligence, clinical quality improvement, and surgical education)
endorsements.quote: Undoubtably more insight into data origin and other changes made to the data along its lifecycle would help to identify and address bias within large datasets.

endorsements.title: Challenges in Implementing the Local Node Infrastructure for a National Federated Machine Learning Network in Radiology
endorsements.quote: Data governance policies and procedures must be established before building an infrastructure for federated learning.

endorsements.title: Health Equity Considerations in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
endorsements.quote: Health and research institutions must regularly evaluate data governance policies that clearly define how patient data, including digital phenotyping and behavioral metadata, are collected, stored, and shared.

endorsements.title: A call for ethical, equitable, and effective artificial intelligence to improve care for all people with epilepsy: A roadmap. A report by the ILAE Global Advocacy Council and Big Data Commission
endorsements.quote: Adopting best practices, such as standardized data governance frameworks, can help ensure that ownership and access are both transparent and ethically managed.

endorsements.title: AI/ML-based strategies for enhancing equity, diversity, and inclusion in randomized clinical trials
endorsements.quote: Implementing this framework demands a robust Data Governance policy to establish data ownership and ensure compliance with global regulations like GDPR and HIPAA.

endorsements.title: The Cardiologist Driving Synthetic AI: The TIMA Method for Clinically Supervised Synthetic Data Generation
endorsements.quote: For this reason, TIMA emphasizes governance structures as a core component of clinically responsible synthetic data generation.

endorsements.title: Prioritizing human-AI collaboration in healthcare: the TRIAD framework for trustworthy governance, real-world, and integrated adaptive deployment
endorsements.quote: Firstly, rigorous data governance is essential, ensuring that training and validation data are high-quality, representative, and handled with strict adherence to privacy regulations like health insurance portability and accountability act (HIPAA) in the United States and general data protection regulation (GDPR) in Europe [ 39 , 40 ].

endorsements.title: AI in Clinical Decision Support Systems: Promising Applications and Strategies for Managing Data Challenges
endorsements.quote: Establish data stewards with clear roles and responsibilities, definitions, quality rules, and catalog curation.

endorsements.title: Rethinking bioinformatics expertise in the era of artificial intelligence
endorsements.quote: Treating data work as scientific work, investing in metadata standards, ontology alignment, provenance tracking, and systematic bias auditing, is therefore not administrative overhead.

endorsements.title: From Data Stewardship to Model Stewardship: Extending Governance Frameworks for AI Era Health Data Use
endorsements.quote: Model stewardship, we propose, should encompass at minimum training data provenance documentation, so downstream users know what populations and practice settings a model reflects; (2) cross-institutional validation before deployment beyond the training context; (3) ongoing monitoring for context drift as clinical practices evolve; and (4) accountability structures that follow the model through its life cycle, not merely the data at its origin.

endorsements.title: Rethinking scale in AI-driven genomic medicine - The role of small biobanks
endorsements.quote: This requires harmonised metadata, versioned variant-calling pipelines, reference-genome documentation, phenotype provenance, ancestry descriptors, consent status, data quality metrics, and clear rules for secondary use.

endorsements.title: Humanoid Colleagues and the Rheumatology Workforce: Preparing for a New Era
endorsements.quote: The profession should define standards for data provenance, auditability, and explainability in rheumatology‐specific AI applications, grounded in medical professionalism and patient safety, rather than leaving these decisions to vendors or regulators.

commentary.bottom_line: Seventeen sources endorse AI data governance with named stewards, a data register, and version-controlled provenance, but no supplied study tests whether these measures improve data quality or patient outcomes. The recommendation rests on expert consensus and framework language, and no study documenting the hazard was supplied either.

perspectives.view: No supplied study tests the practice and none documents the hazard. The support consists of two frameworks using mandatory language (CHAI), one NIST profile, one multi-society guidance statement, and commentaries. Consensus statements of this kind do not enter a GRADE rating, so certainty about benefit cannot be graded.

The CHAI playbooks state that organizations that only deploy vendor models must still keep data preparation procedures for data input to models, used in fine-tuning, or shared with vendors. Several commentaries tie governance to HIPAA and GDPR compliance. These are voluntary frameworks and opinion pieces, and none reports an audit or enforcement outcome.

One commentary on health equity calls for regular review of policies covering how patient data, including behavioral metadata, are collected and shared, and the SAGES statement suggests that provenance records may help detect dataset bias. Neither source reports data showing that governance reduced bias for any population.

commentary.research_gap: No supplied study compares sites with and without named data stewards, a maintained data register, or version-controlled provenance on measures such as data error rates, time to trace a model failure to its source data, or model performance drift. The staffing and cost needed to maintain these structures in a health system are also unmeasured in the supplied evidence.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no test included Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether data governance helps detect or correct data problems affecting these groups remains unstudied, and safety-net systems with limited informatics staff have no evidence on the feasibility of this practice.
